assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a genuine new concept of molecular organisation: membraneless compartments governed by multivalency, thermodynamics and phase behaviour. It reframes cell biology in physical-chemical terms, which is the kind of reduction to general principles I value most.
assessment.attribution: The P-granule droplet work (Brangwynne, Hyman) opened the field; Rosen's multivalent signalling-protein condensates gave the quantitative physical-chemical framework. Pappu and Mittag are important on sequence grammar and the theory side, so the three-person limit leaves real unresolved credit.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed by many independent groups since 2009, and the concept is stable. Its biological generality is still debated, and some disease and function claims are not settled, so recognition is arguably slightly early for the full scope but sound for the core concept.
uncertainties: How much in-cell condensate behaviour is true equilibrium phase separation versus other assemblies is contested.
Allocation among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is not clear-cut.
My recollection of the detailed priority timeline is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are applied lipid self-assembly: pH-dependent charge, fusogenic non-bilayer phases and kinetically controlled mixing yield particles that carry nucleic acids into cells. They underpin mRNA vaccines and siRNA drugs, so the impact is very large and rests on membrane and colloid physical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group developed the lipid-formulation and ionizable-lipid concepts with Hope and Madden and the SNALP route with MacLachlan; Anderson and Langer contributed combinatorial lipidoids. Credit is spread across Vancouver and Boston groups and companies, and the vaccine-enabling mRNA work is already recognised by the 2023 Medicine prize.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale, so confirmation is unusually strong. Timing is good, although the Medicine recognition of mRNA may make the committee hesitate on whether the lipid part is distinct enough for Chemistry.
uncertainties: Whether the delivery-chemistry contribution is seen as separable from the 2023 Medicine prize.
Fair split between ionizable-lipid design, formulation process and the lipidoid work.
Exact individual contributions are from memory and not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to degrade proteins turns small molecules into tools that rewire the ubiquitin-proteasome system, with a new pharmacological logic and clinical candidates. This is a clear conceptual advance in chemistry-driven biology, although I would assess it mostly from a physical-chemical view of ternary complex cooperativity.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced PROTACs, Ciulli added structure-guided design and VHL ligands, and the thalidomide cereblon mechanism (Handa, Ito, others) is a separate molecular-glue strand. A compound candidate with parts needing different credit.
assessment.maturity: Strong mechanistic and growing clinical support, but approved degrader drugs are still few, so long-term therapeutic impact is not yet proven.
uncertainties: Clinical outcome is still pending for most degraders.
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be credited together or separately.
Priority claims among several groups are not resolved here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel view explains how a random heteropolymer finds a unique fold, which is a statistical-mechanical principle of molecular organisation and a landmark of biophysical chemistry. It connects thermodynamics, kinetics and hydrophobic collapse in a way that shaped how a generation thinks about folding.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson set out the funnel theory; Dill contributed lattice models and the hydrophobic-collapse picture; Fersht supplied the experimental mapping, so credit needs a choice between theory and experiment.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are well established and experimentally supported for decades, so maturity is high. AlphaFold-era structure prediction may reduce the perceived urgency, but also stresses how fundamental the physical picture is.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants a theory-only prize or must include Fersht's experiments.
Relative weight of Dill versus Bryngelson and Fersht is uncertain.
Details of priority are from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics made ab initio dynamics practical by combining electronic structure and nuclear motion, and opened first-principles studies of liquids, interfaces and reactions. It is a foundational method that is used across chemistry and materials science.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is unusually clean, with Car and Parrinello as the two authors of the 1985 method. Parrinello also appears under metadynamics and machine-learned potentials, which could complicate how a computational prize is shaped.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of use and independent confirmation make this fully mature. If anything it is a long-overdue recognition, with the risk that the committee prefers a broader computational prize.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with a combined computational-methods prize involving Parrinello.
Whether the committee sees it as superseded by newer methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers of thiols on gold gave a simple, reproducible way to engineer interfaces with molecular precision, and they underpin soft lithography and surface biophysics. As an interface and self-assembly scientist I value the concept highly, as it links intermolecular forces to defined surface structure.
assessment.attribution: Sagiv started silane monolayers, Nuzzo and Allara reported thiol-gold SAMs, and Whitesides developed the broad science and soft lithography. Credit is divided and priority questions are real.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and widely used for decades. The scientific novelty now is historical, so the prize risk is that the discovery is seen as long since absorbed into the field.
uncertainties: Priority among Sagiv, Nuzzo and Allara.
How much soft lithography should be counted as part of this candidate.
Remote concern that recognition is late in terms of the peak of activity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing chemically converts one nucleotide to another in the genome without double-strand breaks, a conceptually clean chemistry-on-DNA invention with large therapeutic reach. It extends CRISPR in a distinct, chemistry-based way.
assessment.attribution: Liu is clearly the central inventor, with Komor and Gaudelli as the lead trainee contributors and Nishida and Kondo as parallel developers; a one-person prize is fair for the idea but it ignores a closely related independent line.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are in progress and a first therapy has been reported, but long-term outcomes are early. Confirmation of the editing chemistry is strong, while durable clinical impact needs time.
uncertainties: Whether prime editing should be counted with it, as Liu would then be sole recipient.
Parallel independent work by Nishida and Kondo.
Premature relative to clinical validation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation methods opened solution structure and dynamics of large biomolecules, including methyl-TROSY for large complexes. It is a physical-chemistry achievement with direct reach into biological dynamics and my own methods area of NMR and scattering.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore are the main drivers, with Wagner, Palmer and others also decisive; the one-to-three limit forces a difficult choice, and Wüthrich already received the 2002 prize for NMR structure determination.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed. Timing risk comes from the earlier NMR prizes and the shift to cryo-EM and AI structure prediction.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for NMR structures.
Who should be excluded among Clore, Wagner and Palmer.
Possible view that it is already well recognised by other awards.
